title: Definite integrals and areas

points.text: Areas where the curve goes below the x-axis, without technology

bigPicture: Definite integrals evaluated by hand give exact areas. Watch for parts of the curve below the x-axis, and for the area between two curves subtract lower from upper.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you evaluate a definite integral by hand?
keyIdeas.answer: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a), where F is any antiderivative (the C cancels).

keyIdeas.cue: Area when the curve goes below the x-axis?
keyIdeas.answer: The integral of a part below the axis is negative. Find the roots, integrate each part separately and add the absolute values: area = ∫|y| dx.
Find the intersection points for the limits, then area = ∫ₐᵇ (upper − lower) dx. Check which curve is on top; if they cross, split there.

keyTerms.def: area above the axis counts +, below counts −

workedExamples.title: Between curves
workedExamples.prompt: Find the area enclosed by y = x² and y = 2x.

misconceptions.wrong: ∫ from −2 to 2 of x³ dx is the area
misconceptions.right: It is 0 because the two parts cancel; the area is 8.
Upper minus lower, or the answer is negative.

practice.prompt: Find the total area enclosed by y = x² − 4x + 3, the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 3.
commonErrors: Subtracting the parts instead of adding

practice.prompt: Find the area of the region enclosed by y = 4 − x² and y = e^x.
commonErrors: Using the x-axis as a boundary
Rounding the limits to 1 d.p. first

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
